name: Solana Foundation Grants (standard, convertible, RFPs)
sectors: Solana public goods; developer tooling, infrastructure, education, open-source; vertical-agnostic (Web3 and AI projects listed); convertible grants for public goods with a commercial component
stage: Idea/pre-seed accepted for public-goods work. Official page: applicants are 'individuals, independent teams, governments, nonprofits, companies, universities, and academics'; convertible grants target 'a project that needs support in building a totally novel proof of concept before being able to raise venture funds'. Reviewed 'on a rolling basis' (review ~1 week, decision ~3 weeks).
check_size: Not published for Foundation grants; milestone-based. Superteam Earn (linked from the page) offers quick equity-free microgrants (page text says ~$10k).
twitter: unknown (not shown on solana.org grants page)
best_channel: Fill the HubSpot grant application form on solana.org/grants-funding, or apply for a Superteam Earn microgrant first.
cold_pitch_policy: 'All funding applicants for Solana Foundation standard and convertible grants are required to fill out the application' ... 'All applications are reviewed on a rolling basis'. Criteria: public good, 'Only Possible on Solana', 'Clear Use of Funds'.
notes: Grants fund public goods only; a closed-source trading bot does not fit a standard grant. A convertible grant may fit if part of the work is an open, reusable component (e.g. open-source Solana prediction-market or trading tooling). Superteam Earn (earn.superteam.fun/grants) advertises 'Equity-Free' fast grants for Solana ideas. Polymarket runs on Polygon, so a Solana grant needs a Solana angle.

name: Colosseum (Solana hackathons, Eternal challenge, Accelerator)
sectors: Solana crypto startups; DeFi, trading, payments, consumer, AI, infrastructure (hackathon winners include trading apps such as PeaksTrade, SynthesisTrade, Tempo_Trade, Darklake)
stage: Idea/pre-seed accepted. The Eternal challenge says 'Launch a product in 4 weeks and compete for $250,000 in pre-seed funding'. Accelerator is for winners only: founders must 'first participate in Eternal or the Colosseum Hackathon'.
check_size: $250,000 per accepted accelerator team ('SAFE + token warrant or Colosseum STAMP structure'); hackathon prizes vary
geography: Global, online; accelerator has 2 weeks in San Francisco
pitch_email_or_form: https://colosseum.com/eternal (sign up, start a 4-week sprint, submit product); https://colosseum.com/hackathon
best_channel: Sign up on colosseum.com, run an Eternal 4-week sprint (window open at verification time, closes in ~4 days), or enter the next hackathon (search result: Sep 28 - Nov 2, 2026).
cold_pitch_policy: 'There's no direct application form - you must compete to gain entry.' 'Submit your crypto product in-between hackathons to be considered for $250,000 in pre-seed funding, acceptance into Colosseum's next accelerator cohort, and the new Eternal Award.'
notes: Two hackathons per year, each followed by an accelerator cohort. Frontier Hackathon 2026 had 2,857 submissions; Cohort 5 has 21 startups. Winner lists on colosseum.com include several trading and prediction-market style products, so a trading-bot product on Solana is in scope. Requires building on Solana.

name: Ethereum Foundation Ecosystem Support Program (ESP)
sectors: Ethereum public goods: builder tools, infrastructure, research, cryptography, education, community; funded through Wishlist items and RFPs
stage: Idea stage accepted for public-goods work: 'Whether you're working on a specific project, or you're still exploring possibilities, you can connect with our team for guidance.' Office Hours give non-financial help before you apply.
check_size: Not published on the official site. Third-party guides (grantedai.com, grantchain.eu) claim roughly $5K-$200K+, small grants up to $30K; unverified.
best_channel: Book Office Hours first, then apply against a matching Wishlist or RFP item on esp.ethereum.foundation.
cold_pitch_policy: 'The work we support is free, open-source, non-commercial, and designed to create positive sum outcomes for the community.' 'Our support is generally directed toward enabling builders rather than end-users.' 'Most applications are reviewed within 3-6 weeks.' Grants 'are paid on-chain in ETH by default'.
notes: Not a fit for a commercial trading bot. Possible fit only for an open-source Ethereum/L2 research or tooling deliverable (e.g. open prediction-market data or agent tooling) that matches a Wishlist item. Funded $44.4M across 677 projects in 2024.

name: Gitcoin Grants (GG rounds, Grants Stack)
sectors: Digital public goods, Ethereum infrastructure, open source, developer tooling, community; quadratic funding with matching pools; partner rounds (e.g. Arbitrum DAO, Base Builder Grants, Polygon Grants are listed as apps on gitcoin.co)
stage: Idea stage possible but funding depends on crowd donations plus matching; projects must meet each round's eligibility (usually open-source public goods). No formal stage requirement found.
check_size: Variable; crowd donations plus quadratic matching. One testimonial on the program page cites $9,000 in a round. Program total '$50,000,000+ Towards Public Goods'.
pitch_email_or_form: Apply via Grants Stack Builder (builder.gitcoin.co per the program page); round schedules on gitcoin.co/campaigns
best_channel: Create a Grants Stack Builder profile and apply to the next GG round (GG25 is referenced on gitcoin.co) or a partner round that fits.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Use Grants Stack's Builder to create a single profile that you can use to apply to all the rounds for which you meet the eligibility criteria.' Rounds have run 'quarterly since 2019'.
notes: GG24 (Oct 2025) used a Domain Allocator model. gitcoin.co home page lists 'GG25, ETHBoulder, Network Goods' as current/upcoming campaign examples; round dates for GG25 not verified. Support KB page is outdated (mentions GG19). Closed-source trading bots are not public goods; only open tooling qualifies. grants.gitcoin.co did not resolve at verification time.

name: Optimism Collective grants (Retro Funding, Grants Council Season 9, OP Atlas)
sectors: Superchain onchain apps, DeFi/DEX liquidity, dev tooling, public goods; Season 9 Grants Council targets 'DEX TVL in Priority Pairs' and 'DEX Fees in Priority Pairs'
stage: Retro Funding is retroactive: 'Your project must have a verified contract on one of the following OP Chains' (includes Base, OP Mainnet, Unichain). Grants Council Season 9 is prospective and lists 'Vaults, strategies, or automation that improve depth for priority pairs' as eligible; idea-stage teams can apply but must target the metrics.
check_size: Retro Funding: Onchain Builders budget 'Up to 8M OP' (Season 7, monthly rewards). Grants Council Season 9 sizes not stated in the thread.
pitch_email_or_form: https://app.opgrants.io/programs/1045/apply (Season 9 Grants Council, applications Feb 11 - May 20, 2026); Retro Funding via OP Atlas project setup at https://atlas.optimism.io/
best_channel: Register the project in OP Atlas, then apply to the current Grants Council mission or enroll for Retro Funding once contracts are live on an OP Chain such as Base.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Apply by the monthly application deadline, and your project will be evaluated for rewards starting the following month.' Grants Council: 'Projects must target one of the following metrics: DEX TVL in Priority Pairs ... DEX Fees in Priority Pairs'.
notes: opgrants.io domain was expired at verification time; app.opgrants.io form link came from the governance forum. Season 9 submissions closed May 20, 2026; watch the forum for Season 10. A market-making or liquidity bot on Base/Unichain fits the Season 9 liquidity theme better than a Polymarket bot. Atlas pages are JavaScript-only and were not readable.

name: Base Ecosystem Fund / Base Batches / Base Builder Grants (Coinbase)
sectors: Onchain businesses on Base: 'Trading, Payments, AI Agents, Other' (fund portfolio filters); Base Batches seeks 'trading, payments, agents, financing, and asset issuance'
stage: Pre-seed and idea stage accepted. Ecosystem Fund: 'we invest in pre-seed and seed stage startups that choose Base as their home'. Base Batches: 'Pre-product to post-MVP teams that have not yet raised a formal Seed round'; the base.org ladder labels Base Batches as '01 Idea' and Ecosystem Fund as '02 Pre-seed & Seed'.
check_size: Base Batches: '$100K investment from the Base Ecosystem Fund' (basebatches.xyz also cites $10k grants for top 15 and $50k investments for min 3 teams). Ecosystem Fund check size not published. Builder Grants: small retroactive ETH grants (third-party: 1-5 ETH).
pitch_email_or_form: https://www.base.org/ecosystem-fund/apply (Ecosystem Fund form: Company, Team, Idea, Funding, Why Base); https://www.base.org/batches/apply (Batch 004: applications open Aug 19, close Sep 9, 2026); Builder Grants nomination form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfXuEzmiAzRhie_z9raFCF1BXweXgVt18o-DvBuRRgyTygL2A/viewform
best_channel: Apply to Base Batches 004 before Sep 9, 2026 (written plus video submission), and submit the Ecosystem Fund form in parallel.
cold_pitch_policy: Ecosystem Fund page: 'Apply' button leads to an open form. Base Batches: 'Applications Open ... This application requires both a written and video submission and does not save drafts.' Builder Grants: 'We will mostly be relying on our own discovery process to find these grantees, but if you want to nominate someone you can submit a nomination'.
notes: Strong fit: explicit 'Trading' and 'AI Agents' portfolio categories; Batch 003 accepted teams include Onsight (social prediction markets), Opal (private DEX), Nivo (onchain FX). Perks include Coinbase Prime, Onramp API, AWS/Alchemy credits. Base is an OP Chain, so Optimism Retro Funding also applies. A Polymarket bot would need a Base deployment or Base-first product.

name: Arbitrum Foundation grants (Audit Program, ArbiFuel, DAO programs)
sectors: Arbitrum dApps and infrastructure; audits; gas sponsorship; gaming (AGV); Orbit rollups (Alchemy); past programs funded DeFi AI agents (Trailblazer 2.0)
stage: Early-stage accepted for active programs: Audit Program is for 'early-stage Arbitrum projects with strong product-market fit'; ArbiFuel is 'to help early-stage teams ship faster, test freely, and onboard users'. The general Arbitrum Foundation Grant Program is marked 'Inactive / Program Complete' with 'Applications will open soon'.
check_size: Audit Program: $10M ARB pool (audit subsidies); ArbiFuel: gas sponsorship; Alchemy-Arbitrum: up to $500K infra credits. Foundation Grant Program historically $20K-$150K (third-party grantedai.com, unverified); Uniswap-Arbitrum program $50K-$250K (complete).
pitch_email_or_form: Audit Program: https://tally.so/r/3xzEzv?program=aap ; ArbiFuel: https://airtable.com/appzb4GfqGfrnDXjW/shrulGIIp6l6ezAlt ; Foundation grant form (program inactive): https://arbitrumfoundation.notion.site/Grant-Application-Form-de318b3dfaea409abbf424c958b3724b ; DAO grants: https://arbitrum.questbook.app
best_channel: Apply to ArbiFuel or the Audit Program now; watch arbitrum.foundation/grants for the Foundation Grant Program to reopen; or submit a DAO proposal on Questbook.
cold_pitch_policy: Foundation Grant Program: 'Our new grant program is coming soon. You can also submit a proposal to the ArbitrumDAO.' Earlier text: 'Applications are being approved on a rolling basis.'
notes: Trailblazer 2.0 ($1M for 'DeFi agents' built with Vibekit) and Trailblazer AI are complete; they show the Foundation funds AI trading agents when active. arbitrum.questbook.app lists Arbitrum DDA 3.0 (domain allocators). Polymarket is on Polygon, so an Arbitrum angle (e.g. perp or DEX trading agents) is required.

name: Uniswap Foundation grants
sectors: Uniswap v4 hooks, Unichain apps and infrastructure, DeFi research, security (audit subsidies via UFSF), governance
stage: Not stated on the site. Programs run 'from concept research to implementation support'; Hook Incubator (Atrium Academy) takes new developers. Idea stage not explicitly confirmed.
check_size: Not published on the site. Third-party (web3grants.fyi) claims $7,500 to $1M+; unverified. Foundation committed $26M in grants in 2025 (CoinDesk).
pitch_email_or_form: https://share.hsforms.com/18Kv3hTvDSt-x1wK9va0OYwsdca9 (the 'Get started' HubSpot form linked from the homepage; purpose not labeled as grant application); Security Fund: https://areta.fillout.com/ufsf-projects
best_channel: Use the homepage 'Get started' form or join the Uniswap Hook Incubator (atrium.academy/uniswap); no dedicated open grant application page was found.
notes: Grants are large, milestone-based and open-source oriented (OpenZeppelin hooks library, Panoptic v4 interface, Gauntlet research). A trading bot fits only as an open v4 hook or Unichain liquidity tool. Unichain is an OP Chain, so Optimism programs also apply.

name: Hack VC
sectors: Crypto, AI, DeFi, web3 infrastructure; portfolio includes Bybit, Kamino, Morpho, EigenLayer, Gauntlet, Amber Group, Grass, 0G
stage: Earliest stages: 'We partner at the earliest stages with founders'. Pre-seed acceptance not stated on the site; third-party (f4.fund) says pre-seed only 'for exceptional teams with significant traction'.
check_size: Not published on the site. Third-party: seed $5M-$10M, Series A $10M-$25M (f4.fund, unverified). $200M fund (TechCrunch 2022).
best_channel: Email contact@hack.vc with a deck, or DM a partner on X; the site has no founder application form.
notes: Runs a quantitative research division with a proprietary trading desk and hack.summit() developer community (third-party). Portfolio has trading and DeFi risk firms (Gauntlet, Amber, Bybit, Kamino), so quant trading is a known theme. Check sizes look above pre-seed.

name: Wintermute Ventures
type: VC firm (strategic arm of a trading firm)
sectors: DeFi and CeFi: trading platforms, exchanges, self-custody, tokenization, stablecoins, data oracles, analytics, infrastructure; portfolio categories include 'Trading Platforms' and 'Data & Analytics'; portfolio: Backpack, Vertex, Bluefin, Chaos Labs, Kiln, Noble, Thalex, Bebop (incubated)
stage: Seed and Series A: 'We invest $0.5M to $5M+ across Seed and Series A stages globally'. Pre-seed not listed; idea stage not explicitly accepted.
pitch_email_or_form: https://wintermuteotc.typeform.com/ventures ('Apply - To get funding and build with us')
best_channel: Submit the Wintermute Ventures Typeform application; the portfolio page links it as the way 'to get funding and build with us'.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Apply: To get funding and build with us' (open form). 'Unlike traditional VCs, Wintermute Ventures exclusively invests its own funds'. 'We focus on investing in companies and protocols at the intersection of financial and enterprise technology'.
notes: Best thesis match for a trading-bot founder: parent firm is one of the largest crypto market makers; they co-build integrations (55+), and incubated Bebop, GMCI and Wildcat. 100+ investments since 2020. Seed minimum ($0.5M) implies a product beyond idea stage.

best_channel: No cold channel published; warm introduction via a portfolio founder or an ecosystem team (e.g. Solana) is the realistic route.

partner_twitters: unknown (GPs are William Nuelle and Mike Giampapa; handles not shown on the site)

name: Framework Ventures
sectors: Crypto/DeFi, AI, robotics, fintech, energy; portfolio: Chainlink, Aave, Synthetix, The Graph, Hyperliquid, Sky, Plasma, Mecka AI, Obex (stablecoin startup incubator)
stage: Leads early-stage rounds, but 'our check sizes typically range from $5m to $50m'; pre-seed or idea stage is not stated and the check size implies seed or later.
pitch_email_or_form: Hello@framework.ventures (labeled 'for founders' on the contact page)
best_channel: Email Hello@framework.ventures with a deck; this is the published founder channel.
cold_pitch_policy: Contact page lists 'for founders: Hello@framework.ventures'. No other policy text found.
notes: Early Hyperliquid backer and deep DeFi history; Obex (Framework-backed) is positioned as a 'Y-Combinator for Stablecoin Startups with $2.5B Mandate' (Forbes). Check size is far above pre-seed, so expect a pass at idea stage unless routed to Obex.

name: Electric Capital
sectors: AI, cryptography, distributed systems, fintech; crypto trading and DeFi portfolio: dYdX, Bullet (Solana trading), Ellipsis Labs (Solana perps), Hashflow, Bitnomial, Curve, Aave, Aerodrome, Auto Finance and Agentic Data Intelligence (AI agents)
stage: Pre-seed accepted: site states 'Stage: Preseed-Series A' and 'We partner closely at preseed and seed as founders develop product-market fit'. Idea stage not explicitly stated.
pitch_email_or_form: info@electriccapital.com ('If you're a founder building frontier technologies, we want to hear from you. Email us at info@electriccapital.com')
best_channel: Email info@electriccapital.com; the contact page invites founders directly.
cold_pitch_policy: 'Are you building in these areas? Get in touch with us at info@electriccapital.com.' 'We support exceptional founders at every stage.'
notes: Engineer-led ('All of our investors are engineers'). Publishes the annual Developer Report. Portfolio has several trading venues and AI-agent finance startups, so an AI trading-agent pitch is on-thesis; $1M minimum check means they expect a fundable pre-seed round, not a solo idea.
